summary: A concentric cutaway, walked from the outside in, ending on the question of how to shape the blast.

paragraphs.text: The Gadget was a sphere built from shells, each with one job. On the outside, {{detonators}} detonators sat in a pattern of points across the surface, ready to fire at the same moment.

Working inward: explosive lenses, an inner explosive charge, an aluminium pusher, a natural-uranium tamper, the plutonium core ({{core_mass}}) and, at the very centre, a polonium-beryllium initiator. The drawing is a schematic, not to scale.
The whole design depends on one problem. Every detonator starts its own spreading wave, but the core needs a single, round wave moving inward. The next scene shows how that is done.

events.detail: The closed sphere opens to a section so the seven layers can be seen.
At the centre sits the plutonium core, {{core_mass}}.
{{detonators}} separate waves must become one round, inward-moving wave.

callouts.text: {{detonators}} detonators sit on the surface, wired to fire at the same instant.
Each lens pairs a fast explosive with a slower insert. Together they shape the detonation wave.
A shell of explosive that the merged wave drives inward as one smooth push.
A smooth aluminium shell that evens out the shock and passes it to the tamper.
Natural uranium. It reflects neutrons back and, by its inertia, holds the core together a moment longer.
{{core_mass}} of plutonium, about the size of an orange. Squeezing it is the whole point.
A polonium-beryllium source at the centre that releases a burst of neutrons when the core is crushed.
{{detonators}} separate explosions each send out a spreading wave. How do you turn them into one perfectly round wave moving inward?
